finding.title: Fix round hard-NULLs suburb max_drop_pct/max_drop_abs, killing a live "Biggest cut" column + sort and pinning a public API field to 0
finding.detail:
The final fix commit (94bee87db, "stop publishing extremes alongside count/mean/median on k-floored rows") replaced `MAX(max_pct)`/`MAX(max_abs)` in `mv_suburb_price_drops` with `NULL::double precision AS max_drop_pct` / `NULL::double precision AS max_drop_abs`. Nothing downstream was updated:

1. `services/shorts/internal/store/shorts/postgres_house_prices.go:696` still offers `sort="max"` as `orderBy = "COALESCE(d.max_drop_pct, 0)"`, so that ordering key is now constant 0 for every row.
2. `web/src/@/components/housing/suburb-price-drops-panel.tsx:57` renders a live "Biggest cut" sort button (used on `/housing` and `/housing/[state]`) that calls `listSuburbPriceDropsClient(stateCode, "max", 25)`.
3. Three surfaces render the value: `suburb-price-drops-panel.tsx:104`, `price-drops/suburb-drops-leaderboard.tsx:60` (the server-rendered, SEO-visible `/price-drops` leaderboard, page.tsx:165), each guarded by `r.maxDropPct > 0 ? … : "—"`.
4. `proto/shortedapi/shorts/v1alpha1/housing.proto:356-357` (`SuburbPriceDrop.max_drop_pct` / `max_drop_abs`, "largest single reduction, AUD") becomes permanently 0 for external API consumers, with no proto/doc change.

The stated k-anon rationale is also applied inconsistently and does not hold on its own terms: the same MV still publishes `median_drop_pct` (line 118) even though `mv_suburb_price_drops` is gated at `dropped_listing_count >= 3` (line 126), and `PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5)` over exactly 3 addresses IS one address's exact drop pct — the very thing the suppression claims to prevent. Meanwhile `mv_state_price_drops` (line 218) still publishes `CASE WHEN d.dropped_count >= 3 THEN d.max_drop_pct END`, i.e. the extreme is retained at the identical k=3 floor for states. So the change removes a working, displayed metric without closing the leak it targets.

The new integration test `postgres_mv_correctness_integration_test.go:171-187` locks the NULLs in, so this ships as intended behaviour unless corrected.
finding.failure_scenario: After 000109 is hand-applied to prod: load `/housing`, click the "Biggest cut" sort button. `ListSuburbPriceDrops(stateCode, "max", 25)` runs `ORDER BY COALESCE(d.max_drop_pct, 0) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 25` where every row's key is 0, so Postgres returns an arbitrary 25 suburbs (not the deepest cutters, and a different set from "Most cuts"), and every cell in the "Biggest cut" column renders "—". The same column is a full row of "—" on the server-rendered `/price-drops` leaderboard and on `/housing/[state]`. A public API consumer of `ListSuburbPriceDrops` reads `max_drop_pct: 0` / `max_drop_abs: 0` for every suburb.
finding.fix: Either restore `MAX(max_pct)`/`MAX(max_abs)` behind the same `CASE WHEN dropped_listing_count >= N THEN …` guard used for the state MV (and pick a consistent N across suburb + state), or remove the metric end-to-end: drop the "max" SortKey and the "Biggest cut" columns from `suburb-price-drops-panel.tsx` / `suburb-drops-leaderboard.tsx`, drop the `case "max"` branch in `ListSuburbPriceDrops`, and deprecate `SuburbPriceDrop.max_drop_pct`/`max_drop_abs` in the proto. If the k-anon concern is real, `median_drop_pct` at n=3 must be suppressed too.

verdict.note:
Verified end-to-end in the worktree; no guard or compensating change exists in 8c120a352..HEAD.

MV: services/migrations/000109_fix_listing_rollup_correctness.up.sql:119-120 emits `NULL::double precision AS max_drop_pct/max_drop_abs` in mv_suburb_price_drops. `git show 94bee87db` confirms it replaced `MAX(max_pct)`/`MAX(max_abs)`; `max_abs` was also removed from the per_source/win/agg CTEs, so it is no longer even computed.

Downstream is untouched:
- services/shorts/internal/store/shorts/postgres_house_prices.go:696 still maps sort="max" to `COALESCE(d.max_drop_pct, 0)`; :713-714 still COALESCE both columns to 0. The branch's diff of this file only touches crime ranks, ListSuburbDropListings and ListAgencyPriceStats.
- services/shorts/internal/services/shorts/house_prices.go:383 still copies MaxDropPct/MaxDropAbs into the response; the handler does not validate `sort`.
- proto/shortedapi/shorts/v1alpha1/housing.proto:343 still documents sort 'count'|'avg'|'max'; :356-357 still document max_drop_pct/max_drop_abs ("largest single reduction, AUD"). No proto/doc change in the branch.
- UI: web/src/@/components/housing/suburb-price-drops-panel.tsx:11,58,77,104 ("Biggest cut" SortKey + button + column) rendered on /housing (page.tsx:261) and /housing/[state] (page.tsx:55); web/src/@/components/housing/price-drops/suburb-drops-leaderboard.tsx:30,60 rendered server-side at web/src/app/price-drops/page.tsx:165. listSuburbPriceDropsClient passes `sort` through unfiltered.

Reachability confirmed: sort=max yields `ORDER BY COALESCE(d.max_drop_pct,0) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 25` over mv_suburb_listing_stats LEFT JOIN mv_suburb_price_drops, so every ordering key ties at 0 -> arbitrary 25 suburbs. The panel (unlike the leaderboard) does not filter droppedListingCount > 0, so the "Biggest cut" tab can even list suburbs with zero cuts; every cell renders "—". API consumers read 0.

Inconsistency claim also holds: the same MV still publishes median_drop_pct (line 105/118) on rows gated at dropped_listing_count >= 3 (line 126) — PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) over exactly 3 values IS one address's value — while mv_state_price_drops:218 retains `CASE WHEN d.dropped_count >= 3 THEN d.max_drop_pct END` at the identical floor.

Locked in by two tests: postgres_mv_correctness_integration_test.go:185-186 (asserts both extremes are NULL) and services/migrations/mv_correctness.test.mjs (asserts the `NULL::double precision AS max_drop_pct/abs` literals).

Severity re-graded and kept at major: no crash, no data leak, and cells degrade to "—", but a live sort control on a flagship public page silently returns an arbitrary suburb set under a "Biggest cut" label, a server-rendered SEO column goes blank across /housing, /housing/[state] and /price-drops, and a documented public API field is pinned to 0 without any proto/doc change. Not a blocker (graceful degradation, no outage); above minor because the ranking is actively misleading.

finding.title: Regression guard against the portal-ID dedup fallback is inert (regex omits the `e.` alias)
finding.detail: `assert.doesNotMatch(up, /source \|\| ':' \|\| listing_id/i)` is meant to prove the `source:listing_id` fallback dedup key was removed from 000109's up migration. But every occurrence of that fallback in this codebase is written with a table alias — `COALESCE(NULLIF(e.address_key, ''), e.source || ':' || e.listing_id)` (000086 up:32/92/187, 000109 down:42/94/165) — and the regex requires `':' || listing_id` with no `e.` prefix. Verified with node: the regex returns false against the real string, while the sibling assertion on line 105 (`/source \|\| ':' \|\| e\.listing_id/i`) returns true. So the guard can never fire.
finding.failure_scenario: A later edit reintroduces `COALESCE(NULLIF(e.address_key, ''), e.source || ':' || e.listing_id) AS dedup_key` into 000109_fix_listing_rollup_correctness.up.sql (restoring the cross-portal double-count the migration exists to remove). `node --test services/migrations/mv_correctness.test.mjs` still reports 4/4 passing.
finding.fix: Match the aliased form, e.g. `/source \|\| ':' \|\| \w*\.?listing_id/i`, mirroring the down-file assertion on line 105.

verdict.note:
CONFIRMED with a correction to the rationale. Reproduced in a sandbox copy (repo untouched).

Core defect is real and reachable exactly as described: at services/migrations/mv_correctness.test.mjs:102, `assert.doesNotMatch(up, /source \|\| ':' \|\| listing_id/i)` cannot see the aliased form `COALESCE(NULLIF(e.address_key, ''), e.source || ':' || e.listing_id) AS dedup_key` (the regex requires listing_id with no `e.` prefix). Injecting that expression back into the `ev` CTE of mv_suburb_price_drops in 000109_fix_listing_rollup_correctness.up.sql — both as a bare dedup_key swap and as a full regression that ALSO removes that CTE's `AND NULLIF(pl.address_key, '') IS NOT NULL` filter — still yields 4 pass / 0 fail. Nothing backstops it: line 101's address_key assertion is a `match`, satisfied by the three untouched MVs; line 103's join assertion is unaffected.

Correction: the DETAIL's supporting claim that "every occurrence of that fallback in this codebase is written with a table alias" and that "the guard can never fire" is FALSE. Four occurrences are unaliased — 000086_price_drops_rollups.up.sql:63 and :124, 000109_fix_listing_rollup_correctness.down.sql:73 and :125, all of the form `COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(NULLIF(address_key, ''), source || ':' || listing_id))`. Injecting that unaliased form into the up file DOES trip the guard (3 pass / 1 fail on doesNotMatch). So the guard is partially effective, blind only to the aliased dedup_key form — which is nonetheless the exact expression the migration exists to remove.

Proposed fix regex /source \|\| ':' \|\| \w*\.?listing_id/i verified to match both aliased and unaliased forms.

Severity stays minor: test-guard gap only. Migration 000109 itself is correct (all four MVs use `pl.address_key AS dedup_key` plus `NULLIF(...) IS NOT NULL`); no production query or MV output is affected. Cost is a silent regression window on a future edit.

finding.title: mv_suburb_price_drops hard-NULLs max_drop_pct/max_drop_abs but the read path and UI still publish them
finding.detail:
The rebuilt `mv_suburb_price_drops` emits `NULL::double precision AS max_drop_pct` / `AS max_drop_abs` (lines 119-120), yet nothing downstream was changed to match:

- `services/shorts/internal/store/shorts/postgres_house_prices.go:713-714` still selects `COALESCE(d.max_drop_pct, 0), COALESCE(d.max_drop_abs, 0)` and maps them onto `SuburbPriceDrop.max_drop_pct/max_drop_abs`.
- `postgres_house_prices.go:696` still whitelists `sort="max"` -> `orderBy = "COALESCE(d.max_drop_pct, 0)"`.
- `web/src/@/components/housing/price-drops/suburb-drops-leaderboard.tsx:60` renders a `Biggest cut` column from `r.maxDropPct`, and `web/src/@/components/housing/suburb-price-drops-panel.tsx:58,104` exposes a `Biggest cut` sort button (server-side: `listSuburbPriceDropsClient(stateCode, sort, limit)`) plus the same column.

finding.failure_scenario: After 000109 is hand-applied to prod, every row of the flagship `/price-drops` leaderboard renders `Biggest cut` as "—" (the column is permanently dead), and clicking "Biggest cut" on the `/housing` SuburbPriceDropsPanel issues `sort=max`, which the store turns into `ORDER BY COALESCE(d.max_drop_pct, 0) DESC NULLS LAST` — a constant 0 for every row — so the user gets an arbitrary heap-order list presented as a ranking by biggest cut.
finding.fix: Either keep publishing the suburb extremes (the MV already enforces a >=3 dropped-address floor, and the state MV publishes the same figure), or drop `max_drop_pct`/`max_drop_abs` from the proto/store/UI and remove the `max` sort option — don't leave a live column and sort key wired to a constant NULL.

verdict.note: Verified in worktree shorted-hw-mv-correctness. 000109 up-migration lines 119-120 do emit `NULL::double precision AS max_drop_pct` / `AS max_drop_abs` in mv_suburb_price_drops (introduced by HEAD commit 94bee87db, "stop publishing extremes alongside count/mean/median on k-floored rows"). ListSuburbPriceDrops still has `case "max": orderBy = "COALESCE(d.max_drop_pct, 0)"` (postgres_house_prices.go:696) and still selects `COALESCE(d.max_drop_pct, 0), COALESCE(d.max_drop_abs, 0)` (713-714), mapped to proto at house_prices.go:383. finding.title: Address-dedup DISTINCT ON has no unique tiebreak, so published asking/sold prices flip between refreshes
finding.detail:
`asking_addresses` (line 24), `sold_addresses` (line 50), `active_addresses` (line 176) and the state `sold_addresses` (line 205) all pick one row per `address_key` with `ORDER BY pl.address_key, pl.last_seen_at DESC, pl.source` (plus `st.sold_at DESC` for sold). None of these keys is unique for two listings from the SAME portal at the same address:

- `last_seen_at` is set to the run timestamp for every listing in a sweep (`services/house-price-collector/crawl_listings_store.go:151,170` — `runTs` is bound to `$22` for both `first_seen_at` and `last_seen_at`), so it is identical across all listings of a sweep.
- `pl.source` is identical for two REA (or two Domain) adverts at the same address.
- Nothing dedups same-source duplicates at write time: the only uniqueness is `UNIQUE (source, listing_id)` (000076), and a relist under a fresh `listing_id` leaves the old row `is_active = true` until a delist sweep, which per the REA truncation behaviour effectively never completes.

The author clearly knew about this class of tie — `mv_agency_stats.base` (line 268) appends `pl.listing_id` as a final tiebreak — but the other four DISTINCT ONs did not get one. The pre-000109 definitions aggregated over all rows (`AVG(price)` over every for-sale listing), so they were deterministic; this diff introduces the non-determinism.

Reproduced on PG14 with the migration applied, two active `rea` rows at `address_key='dup-addr'` with identical `last_seen_at` and prices 2,000,000 / 1,500,000, running the exact `asking_addresses` CTE:
  pick #1 -> 2000000
  (touch the other row so its tuple relocates)
  pick #2 -> 1500000
  pick #3 -> 2000000
finding.failure_scenario: A suburb contains one address advertised twice on realestate.com.au (relist under a new listing_id, old row still is_active) at $2.0M and $1.5M. Two consecutive `refresh_housing_materialized_views()` runs over unchanged listing data publish different `avg_asking`/`median_asking` for that suburb (and different `for_sale_count`/`total_active_listings` if the two rows disagree on `listing_status`), because the DISTINCT ON tie is resolved by physical row order. The same applies to `avg_sold`/`median_sold` via `sold_addresses` and to every state/national aggregate built on `active_addresses`.
finding.fix: Append a unique final tiebreak (`pl.listing_id` or `pl.id`) to the ORDER BY of `asking_addresses`, `sold_addresses` (both copies) and `active_addresses`, matching what `mv_agency_stats.base` already does.

verdict.note:
Real and reachable. The four DISTINCT ON CTEs (000109 lines 24, 50, 176, 205) end at `pl.source` with no unique tiebreak, while `mv_agency_stats.base` (252-253) appends `pl.listing_id` — inconsistent within the same migration. Only uniqueness on property_listings is UNIQUE(source, listing_id) (000076), and `runTs` is one timestamp per run bound to $22 for both first_seen_at/last_seen_at (crawl_listings_store.go:151,201; crawl_listings.go:286), so every row re-sighted in one sweep shares an identical last_seen_at. Cross-portal dupes are broken by `pl.source`; two SAME-portal adverts at one address_key seen in the same sweep tie completely.

Reproduced on PG16 with the exact asking_addresses CTE (3 addresses, one with two tied rea rows at 2.0M/1.5M): avg_asking 1,233,333 -> `UPDATE ... SET updated_at = now()` on the winner (exactly what every re-sight upsert does) -> 1,066,667 -> touch the other -> 1,233,333. Pure tuple relocation, no price change.

Measured against prod (read-only): 73,672 active addressed rows; 905 fully-tied (address_key, source, last_seen_at) groups among for_sale/under_offer; 562 of them have divergent prices, spanning 168 of 500 suburbs. Per-suburb worst-case avg_asking swing mean ~$7.7k, p90 ~$19.8k, max ~$82.7k. Sold side nearly clean (4 divergent groups). Suburb list ORDER BY st.avg_asking (postgres_house_prices.go:698) means ranking can reorder too. mv_correctness.test.mjs is text-assertion only; no determinism coverage.

Three corrections to the write-up that do NOT defeat it: (1) the stated trigger "relist under a fresh listing_id, old row still active" does not actually tie — markAbsent (crawl_listings_store.go:256-267) never bumps last_seen_at, so the stale row is strictly older and the fresh row wins deterministically; the tie requires both adverts live in the SAME sweep (905 such groups exist in prod). (2) total_active_listings cannot flip — suburb MV uses COUNT(DISTINCT address_key) (line 110) and state MV counts already-deduped addresses (line 179); suburb for_sale_count is also stable since the status filter precedes the DISTINCT ON. What flips: for_sale_priced/avg_asking/median_asking (suburb), for_sale_count/for_sale_priced/avg_asking/median_asking (state, status+price projected from the winner), avg_sold/median_sold, and list ordering. (3) "over unchanged listing data" is over-tight — the flip needs tuple relocation, which every crawl run produces (updated_at = now() on each re-sight, markAbsent, HOT prune/vacuum) before each refresh.

Severity stays major: published price statistics for ~34% of tracked suburbs are irreproducible run-to-run, pre-000109 definitions were deterministic (they averaged over all rows), and the fix is a one-token ORDER BY addition. Nothing modified; scratch DB dropped.

finding.title: State rollup is driven off active-only addresses, so sold-only states vanish while their sales stay in the national row
finding.detail:
`mv_state_price_drops` is now `FROM l LEFT JOIN d USING (state_code) LEFT JOIN sold USING (state_code)` (lines 230-232), where `l` is built exclusively from `active_addresses` (`WHERE pl.is_active`, line 172). The previous 000086 definition built `l` from all `property_listings` in the state, so any state with data at all had a row.

Two consequences:
1. A state with no currently-active addressable listing produces no row at all, but its sold addresses still feed the `()` grouping set, so the `AU` row counts sales that no state row accounts for.
2. `suburbs_tracked` (line 185) now counts only suburbs holding a currently-active address, while `sold_count` on the same row spans suburbs that no longer do.

Reproduced on PG14 (NSW: 5 active + 3 sold-inactive; VIC: 3 sold-inactive only):
  000109:      AU total_active=5 sold_count=6 suburbs_tracked=1 | NSW sold_count=3 | (no VIC row)
  000109 down: AU total_active=5 sold_count=6 suburbs_tracked=3 | NSW sold_count=3 | VIC sold_count=3
finding.failure_scenario: `/price-drops` renders the national pulse tile from the `AU` row and the state board from the per-state rows. With a state whose crawled listings have all been delisted, the national tile reports 6 sales while the state board rows sum to 3, and the "N tracked metro suburbs" sub-label drops to the number of suburbs that happen to hold a live advert at refresh time rather than the suburbs the sold figures came from.
finding.fix: Build `l` from the full state universe (or full-outer-join `l`/`sold` on state_code) so the per-state rows still cover states/suburbs that only have sold history, and derive `suburbs_tracked` from the same universe the sold/asking figures come from.

verdict.note:
CONFIRMED at the SQL level, reproduced exactly; the described UI symptom is wrong and the vanishing-state branch is not prod-reachable, so severity stays minor.

VERIFIED FACTS
1. services/migrations/000109_fix_listing_rollup_correctness.up.sql:230-232 is `FROM l LEFT JOIN d USING (state_code) LEFT JOIN sold USING (state_code)`, with `l` built only from `active_addresses` (`WHERE pl.is_active`, line 173). The 000086 original built `l` from `property_listings` with per-metric `FILTER (WHERE is_active ...)`, so every state with any listing had a row.
2. The active and sold populations are disjoint by construction: services/house-price-collector/crawl_listings_store.go:209 `statusActive(status) = status != "sold" && status != "withdrawn"` is bound to `is_active` in the upsert (line 201), so every `listing_status='sold'` row is `is_active=false`. `sold_addresses` can therefore never be covered by `active_addresses` at row level.
3. Reproduced on PG16 (scratch container, schemas dropped afterwards; worktree unmodified) with the reviewer's fixture (NSW 5 active for_sale + 3 sold-inactive in a second suburb; VIC 3 sold-inactive only) - numbers match the finding exactly:
   000109 up:   AU total_active=5 sold_count=6 suburbs_tracked=1 | NSW sold_count=3 suburbs_tracked=1 | NO VIC ROW
   000109 down: AU total_active=5 sold_count=6 suburbs_tracked=3 | NSW sold_count=3 suburbs_tracked=2 | VIC sold_count=3 avg_sold=950000
4. Supporting evidence it is an oversight, not intent: the sibling MV in the SAME migration, `mv_suburb_listing_stats`, uses `FROM fs FULL OUTER JOIN sold USING (region_code)` (line 68) and does keep sold-only suburbs - my run returned `SUBURB:VIC-S for_sale_count=0 sold_count=3`. Only the state rollup drops that universe.
5. The repo's own new fixture already contains the shape: services/shorts/internal/store/shorts/postgres_mv_correctness_integration_test.go:87-89 seeds `SUBURB:NSW-SOLD` with three sold-inactive listings and no active ones, so NSW's `suburbs_tracked` omits a suburb its `sold_count=3` counts (asserted at line 211).
6. `national.sold_count` is a published field: services/shorts/internal/services/shorts/house_prices.go:650-655 maps `SoldCount` onto the `AU` row of the public `GetPriceDropsOverview` response.

WHERE THE FINDING OVERSTATES
- The failure scenario's UI claim is factually wrong. web/src/@/components/housing/price-drops/national-pulse.tsx renders only droppedCount, medianDropPct, droppedValue, droppedShare, totalActiveListings and suburbsTracked; there is no national sold-count tile, so "the national tile reports 6 sales while the state board rows sum to 3" cannot be seen on /price-drops. The AU-vs-states sold mismatch is observable only via the public RPC payload or by manually summing the state board's `(soldCount)` cells.
- Drops are unaffected: the `ev` CTE (line 146) also requires `pl.is_active`, so every state present in `d` is present in `l`. Only `sold` and `suburbs_tracked` are impacted.
- Consequence 1 (state row disappears) needs a state with zero currently-active addressable listings but >=1 sold address in 12 months. With the 115-suburb catalog across the five mainland capitals, that is unreachable for NSW/VIC/QLD/WA/SA; it can only bite a stray/mis-extracted state_code (TAS/ACT/NT) whose few rows are all sold - and there the 000086 behaviour was arguably worse (it published a single sale's median_sold with no k-anon floor, which 000109's `sold_count >= 3` gate now suppresses).
- Consequence 2 (suburbs_tracked universe) is unconditionally live on every row including AU, but the sub-label sits on the "Share of listings cut" tile whose numerator and denominator are both active-scoped, so the tightened active-only count is at least as defensible as the old all-time count; in prod the delta is near zero since every crawled metro suburb holds active addressable stock.

SEVERITY: minor confirmed. Real, reproducible, and internally inconsistent with the suburb MV in the same migration, but with no rendered-UI failure and no prod-reachable state disappearance today. The proposed fix (full-outer-join l/sold on state_code, mirroring line 68, and deriving suburbs_tracked from that union) is the right shape and cheap.

finding.title: refreshHousingMV uses session-scoped SET instead of SET LOCAL on a shared transaction pooler
finding.detail: `refreshHousingMV` sends `SET statement_timeout = 0;\nSELECT refresh_housing_materialized_views()` as one simple-protocol command (also at `services/jobs/internal/jobs/houseprices/store.go:129`). The mechanism itself is correct — I verified on PG14 with `ALTER DATABASE ... SET statement_timeout='500ms'` that a bare `SELECT pg_sleep(2)` is cancelled, that the multi-statement form with the leading `SET` completes, and that the function-level `ALTER FUNCTION ... SET statement_timeout TO '0'` alone does NOT save it. But `SET` (not `SET LOCAL`) is session-scoped and survives the implicit transaction; `connect()` in the same file (line 40) pins `pgx.QueryExecModeSimpleProtocol` precisely because this pool talks to the Supabase transaction pooler on 6543, where server connections are handed back to a shared pool after each transaction. `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 0` works identically inside the implicit block (verified: `current_setting('statement_timeout')` returns `0`) and is scoped to the transaction.
finding.failure_scenario: After a housing collector run, the pooled Supabase server connection it used is returned to the transaction pooler still carrying `statement_timeout = 0`; the next tenant of that server connection runs with no statement timeout, so a runaway query from an unrelated service is never cancelled.
finding.fix: Use `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 0;` in both `refreshHousingMV` copies so the override dies with the transaction.

verdict.note:
Verified in /Users/benebsworth/projects/.worktrees/shorted-hw-mv-correctness (HEAD 94bee87db, diff vs 8c120a352). The finding stands; I could not refute it.

Code as written (identical in both copies — /Users/benebsworth/projects/.worktrees/shorted-hw-mv-correctness/services/house-price-collector/store.go:125-131 and .../services/jobs/internal/jobs/houseprices/store.go:125-131; `diff` reports the files byte-identical):

    _, err := pool.Exec(ctx, `SET statement_timeout = 0;
    		SELECT refresh_housing_materialized_views()`)

Refutation attempts, all failed:

1. "The SET is rolled back with the implicit transaction." REFUTED empirically on local PG17 (psql, two `-c` commands = two implicit transactions on one session, baseline armed via `PGOPTIONS=-c statement_timeout=500ms`):
   - `SET statement_timeout = 0; SELECT current_setting(...)` → inside `0`, and the NEXT command on the same session still reports `0` (leaked).
   - `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 0; SELECT ...` → inside `0`, next command back to `500ms` (scoped), no "SET LOCAL can only be used in transaction blocks" warning.
2. "The proposed fix would break the actual purpose." REFUTED: `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 0; SELECT pg_sleep(2); SELECT 'slept-ok'` completes under a 500ms baseline, while the bare `SELECT pg_sleep(2)` control is cancelled with `canceling statement due to statement timeout`. So SET LOCAL is a drop-in that preserves the fix's intent.
3. "A guard elsewhere in the diff resets it." REFUTED: no `RESET statement_timeout` on any caller path (`grep` over the repo finds only migration down-files); migration 000107's `ALTER FUNCTION refresh_housing_materialized_views() SET statement_timeout TO '0'` is function-scoped and on exit restores the value in effect at call time — which is now 0 because the session SET already ran. `connect()` (store.go:34-42) sets only DefaultQueryExecMode + MaxConns=4; no pgxpool BeforeAcquire/AfterRelease hook.
4. "The pool isn't really a shared transaction pooler." REFUTED: store.go:39 comment plus docs/housing-architecture.md:140/460-469 pin the collector to `…pooler.supabase.com:6543`; terraform/modules/shorts-api/variables.tf:36-38, terraform/modules/chat-service/variables.tf:84-86 and terraform/environments/{dev,prod}/variables.tf:50-52 default the API and chat service to the same 6543 pooler on the same project, so server connections are shared.
5. "Baseline is already 0, so the leak is a no-op." REFUTED by the repo's own incident record: services/migrations/000095_harden_mv_refresh.up.sql:6/34-43 and services/short-data-sync/main.py:321-326 document a real non-zero prod default that cancelled a >2min MV refresh (19 days of stale /statistics + /scans), and 000105_add_aec_donations.up.sql:681 says "prod's pooler default kills" the refresh. So `0` genuinely overwrites an armed non-zero default.

Only residual unknown (why severity stays minor, not major): whether Supabase's Supavisor issues a session reset between transactions. PgBouncer's documented behaviour is that `server_reset_query`/DISCARD ALL does NOT run in transaction mode (`server_reset_query_always=0` default) and SET/RESET is listed as unsupported there precisely because state leaks; Supavisor's per-connection prepared-statement support in transaction mode is inconsistent with issuing DISCARD ALL between transactions. I could not prove that against the live pooler (a pgx-based repro against the local Postgres was blocked by the sandbox's network restriction — the psql evidence above covers the same SQL semantics).

Impact bound: at most `MaxConns = 4` server connections poisoned per collector/crawl run, until the pooler recycles them; the consequence is a missing safety net (another service's runaway query never cancelled), not wrong data. Nothing user-visible.

Fix note for whoever applies it: `services/migrations/mv_correctness.test.mjs:44-56` pins the exact caller string with `/SET statement_timeout\s*=\s*0;\s*SELECT refresh_housing_materialized_views\(\)/i` for BOTH copies, so that regex must be updated in the same change (it happens to still match `SET LOCAL statement_timeout = 0` only if the regex is loosened — as written, `SET LOCAL …` fails it). Same session-scoped pattern pre-exists (out of scope for this diff) at services/short-data-sync/main.py:325.

finding.title: 196 of the 1,165 un-404'd sitemap URLs render "Price not tracked" — the sitemap's price gate reads a different row than the page does
finding.detail: The sitemap selects suburbs with `.filter((s) => s.latestMedianPrice > 0) // only real price data (avoid thin pages)` from `ListStateSuburbs`, but the page renders `GetSuburbProfile`. Both LEFT JOIN `house_price_regions r ON r.sal_code = d.sal_code AND r.region_type='suburb'`, and that table now holds TWO rows per crawled suburb — the Valuer-General key (`SUBURB:VIC-ASCOT VALE`) and a crawl-derived key (`SUBURB:VIC-3032-ASCOT-VALE`). `ListStateSuburbs` fans out to two rows (one priced, one 0) so the sitemap filter sees the priced one; `GetSuburbProfile` (postgres_house_prices.go:365-435) has `LIMIT 1` and picks the crawl row, whose only prices carry `source_licence='proprietary-tos-restricted'` and are filtered out. Verified live against api.shorted.com.au: ListStateSuburbs VIC returns salCode 20075 twice — `SUBURB:VIC-ASCOT VALE` @ 1,300,000 and `SUBURB:VIC-3032-ASCOT-VALE` @ 0; GetSuburbProfile(20075) returns the latter with no latestMedianPrice, and GetHousePriceSeries for that region_code returns zero points (the VG key returns a full series from 2014). Same for 20123 Balwyn and 40002 Adelaide. Counted over the full corpus: 130 of 739 priced VIC slugs and 66 of 426 priced SA slugs are duplicated this way = 196 of the 1,165 URLs this branch restores. A non-duplicated control (20002 Abbotsford) correctly returns 1,232,500, confirming the mechanism.
finding.failure_scenario: After merge the sitemap emits https://shorted.com.au/housing/vic/ascot-vale (selected because ListStateSuburbs says median = $1.3M). Googlebot fetches it; suburb-profile.tsx:106 computes `priced = s.latestMedianPrice > 0` = false, the banner stat renders "Price not tracked", the "Estimate repayments" link is dropped, and chartRegion = 'SUBURB:VIC-3032-ASCOT-VALE' feeds HousingSeriesChart an empty series. Repeats for /housing/vic/balwyn, /housing/sa/adelaide and 193 other flagship metro suburbs.
finding.fix: Either de-duplicate `house_price_regions` for `region_type='suburb'` (one row per sal_code, preferring the open-licence VG key), or make GetSuburbProfile's join deterministic — join through the region that actually has non-proprietary `house_prices` rows (e.g. `ORDER BY (h.value IS NOT NULL) DESC` in a LATERAL, not a bare LIMIT 1). Until then the sitemap gate should be evaluated with the same query the page uses.

verdict.note: Reproduced end to end. Code: web/src/app/sitemap.ts:544 gates on ListStateSuburbs' latestMedianPrice>0 while the page renders GetSuburbProfile; services/shorts/internal/store/shorts/postgres_house_prices.go LEFT JOINs house_price_regions on (sal_code, region_type='suburb') in BOTH queries, but the list query fans out per matching region while GetSuburbProfile ends in a bare LIMIT 1 with no ORDER BY, and both price LATERALs exclude source_licence='proprietary-tos-restricted'. The duplicate key is structural: services/house-price-collector/crawl_targets.go:568 mints SUBURB:<ST>-<POSTCODE>-<SUBURB>, crawl_listings.go:918 upserts it with RegionType "suburb", and store.go:136 linkSuburbSalCodes bridges its sal_code by name — two region_type='suburb' rows per crawled suburb sharing one sal_code. Live prod (read-only POSTs): VIC 3,076 rows / 2,946 distinct SALs, 130 duplicated, 739 priced, all 130 duplicated SALs priced; SA 1,764 / 1,698, 66 duplicated, 426 priced, all 66 priced; NSW 0 priced. 739+426=1,165 and 130+66=196 — the reviewer's counts reproduce exactly. GetSuburbProfile returned the crawl row with no price for 6/6 duplicated SALs sampled (20075 Ascot Vale, 20123 Balwyn, 20214 Bentleigh, 20314 Box Hill, 20224 Berwick, 40002 Adelaide); non-duplicated control 20002 Abbotsford returned 1,232,500. GetHousePriceSeries on SUBURB:VIC-3032-ASCOT-VALE = 0 points vs 11 for SUBURB:VIC-ASCOT VALE. Attribution to this branch is fair: every priced row has an empty postcode, so pre-branch the sitemap emitted "ascot-vale-" while resolveSuburbSalCode matched "ascot-vale" (404); the branch's shared suburbSlug + trailing-hyphen tolerance un-404s all 1,165, newly exposing the 196. No guard in the diff: page.tsx sets no noindex, canonicalSlug equals the sitemap slug so the new permanentRedirect does not fire, and suburb-profile.tsx:105-106 derives `priced` only from data.summary (the stateList query feeds the "nearby" list only), so the banner shows "Price not tracked", the repayments link is dropped, and chartRegion (crawl key) mounts HousingSeriesChart on an empty series instead of the empty-state copy. Severity major, not blocker: no crash or leak and 969/1,165 URLs are correct, but the 196 are the crawled flagship metro suburbs and they defeat the filter's own "avoid thin pages" contract. Root cause is data/backend, fixable without reverting the URL repair (dedupe house_price_regions for region_type='suburb' preferring the open-licence VG key, or make GetSuburbProfile's region pick deterministic via a LATERAL preferring the region with non-proprietary house_prices rows).

finding.title: The new `next:{revalidate:86400}` tag never actually caches a Connect POST — every suburb regeneration re-downloads the whole state index
finding.detail: `suburbIsrFetch` is documented as making the suburb RPCs "explicitly cacheable", and getHousing.test.ts:173-190 asserts the tag is forwarded. But connect-web serialises unary JSON bodies to a `Uint8Array` (`createJsonSerialization().serialize` → `textEncoder.encode(json)`, connect/dist/cjs/protocol/serialization.js:139-147). Next 14.2.13's `IncrementalCache.fetchCacheKey` (next/dist/server/lib/incremental-cache/index.js:227) branches on `typeof init.body.keys === 'function'` — true for any TypedArray — treats it as FormData and calls `formData.getAll(key)`, which throws `TypeError: getAll is not a function` (verified in node). patch-fetch.js:388-394 swallows it, logs "Failed to generate cache key for", leaves cacheKey undefined and runs the fetch uncached. The tag IS still required (without it serverFetchWithUserAgent forces `cache:'no-store'`, which trips trackDynamicFetch and throws DynamicServerError during static generation), so ISR itself is fine — but the caching benefit does not exist. Measured payloads from prod: VIC 2.2 MB, SA 1.2 MB, NSW 3.2 MB — VIC and NSW also exceed Vercel's 2 MB data-cache item cap, so the fetch would be rejected even if keying worked. sitemap.ts:180-183 already documents this exact hazard for connect transports.
finding.failure_scenario: Cold /housing/vic/<suburb> request after the 24h window: resolveSuburbSalCode issues a ListStateSuburbs POST that pulls and JSON-parses 3,076 suburb objects (2.2 MB) from Cloud Run before the page can render, logging "Failed to generate cache key" each time. The suburb's opengraph-image route is a separate request and pays it again. Across 1,165 suburb pages this is ~2.5 GB/day of avoidable Cloud Run egress at full ISR turnover, and the assertion in getHousing.test.ts:173 cannot detect it.
finding.fix: Wrap resolveSuburbSalCode's state index in `unstable_cache` (the sanctioned pattern the repo already uses via `serverFetchOutsideNextCache`) instead of relying on the fetch-level tag, or resolve the SAL with a targeted `listStateSuburbs(stateCode, query, 1)`-style lookup rather than pulling all ~4.5k rows. Keep the `next` tag purely as the no-store guard and correct the comment/test to say so.

verdict.note: Every link verified against installed deps and prod. (1) connect-web 2.1.0 unary sends `body = serialize(msg)` = Uint8Array (connect-transport.js; serialization.js `textEncoder.encode(json)`). (2) Installed Next is 14.2.13; `incremental-cache/index.js` fetchCacheKey branches on `typeof init.body.keys === "function"`, true for TypedArray — reproduced live against the installed package: `THREW: TypeError formData.getAll is not a function`. (3) patch-fetch.js:389-395 catches it, logs "Failed to generate cache key for", leaves cacheKey undefined; both the incrementalCache.get block and the .set are gated on `cacheKey`, so the fetch is fully uncached. (4) The tag IS still load-bearing exactly as the reviewer says — config.ts:267 only forces `cache:'no-store'` when `next === undefined`, so ISR itself is fine; only the caching claim in the comment is false. (5) No other guard: listStateSuburbs/getSuburbProfile have no unstable_cache and no KV key (kv-cache.ts has no suburb-index entry); React cache() dedupes only within one request, and opengraph-image.tsx:50 is a separate request that repeats the pull. (6) Prod measurements match the finding almost exactly: VIC 2,344,439 B / 3,076 suburbs, SA 1,290,384 B / 1,764, NSW 3,355,213 B / 4,544; priced suburbs (the sitemap corpus) = 739 VIC + 426 SA = 1,165, the reviewer's exact number. (7) `npx jest src/app/actions/__tests__/getHousing.test.ts` passes 10/10 including the "ISR-cacheable" test, which only asserts the `next` option reaches a bodyless fetch mock — it cannot detect the keying failure. Repo already documents the same hazard at sitemap.ts:180-183 and config.ts:172-173. Minor nit in the reviewer's framing: NSW contributes 0 sitemap URLs (0 priced), so the 1,165 regenerations all pull the VIC or SA index; the 3.2 MB NSW index is only paid on direct/crawled /housing/nsw/* hits. Severity stays minor: no correctness or user-visible failure, ISR works, and the pre-diff code was worse (fully dynamic) — the defect is a false invariant asserted in a comment plus a test, ~2.3 GB per full ISR turnover of avoidable Cloud Run egress (doubled by the OG route), a multi-MB JSON parse per cold suburb render, and a console.error per RPC. Proposed fix (unstable_cache via serverFetchOutsideNextCache, or a targeted single-suburb lookup) is the right direction.

finding.title: The new `next:{revalidate:86400}` tag cannot cache the resolution fetch — the payload is over Vercel's 2 MB data-cache limit
finding.detail: `suburbIsrFetch` is applied to `listStateSuburbs` (line 132), which is the slug->SAL resolution path for every suburb render. Measured against prod today: NSW 3,355,213 bytes / 816 ms, QLD 2,406,644, VIC 2,344,439 (4,544 / 3,235 / 3,076 rows). Next stores fetch-cache entries as base64 inside a JSON envelope and hard-drops anything over 2 MB — `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/incremental-cache/index.js:382-391` (`if (ctx.fetchCache && !hasCustomCacheHandler && itemSize > 2*1024*1024) { ...; return; }`), with the failure swallowed by the `catch` in `patch-fetch.js:475`. So for all 8 states the write is silently discarded and nothing is ever read back. The tag is still load-bearing (without it `serverFetchWithUserAgent` forces `cache:'no-store'` on the POST and throws DynamicServerError during static generation), but the comment ("These requests must be explicitly cacheable") and the new test (`getHousing.test.ts` "marks suburb list and profile RPC fetches as ISR-cacheable") assert only that the tag is passed, not that anything is cached. Net effect: each of the 15,345 suburb URLs re-downloads its entire state on every ISR (re)generation. The sibling `web/src/app/housing/[state]/[suburb]/opengraph-image.tsx` amplifies it — it exports `revalidate = 86400` but has no `generateStaticParams`, so per the project's own recorded landmine ("Dynamic segment ISR requires generateStaticParams to EXIST (even returning []) — without it revalidate is inert, route renders per-request") it runs the same full-state pull on every single card fetch.
finding.failure_scenario: Googlebot crawls the 1,165 priced suburb URLs plus their OG cards after a revalidate window expires. Each page generation issues a fresh 2.3 MB ListStateSuburbs, and each OG fetch issues another one uncached — roughly 3-5 GB of Cloud Run egress and ~800 ms added to every cold TTFB, for a lookup that needs one row. A full 15,345-URL crawl is ~38 GB.
finding.fix: Resolve the slug with a narrow lookup instead of the whole state: add a `ResolveSuburbSlug(state, slug) -> sal_code` rpc (or reuse `ListStateSuburbs` with `query=` set so the response is a handful of rows and fits the 2 MB data cache), and give the OG route a `generateStaticParams` so its resolution is cached too.

verdict.note:
CONFIRMED on effect, REFUTED on mechanism; severity downgraded major -> minor because the diff makes this strictly cheaper than the base commit.

VERIFIED TRUE (the defect): /Users/benebsworth/projects/.worktrees/shorted-hw-web-suburbs/web/src/app/actions/getHousing.ts:305 resolveSuburbSalCode calls listStateSuburbs(state,"",5000) and there is no KV / unstable_cache layer on it (unlike getHousingOverview and the price-drops actions), while react cache() only dedupes within a single render. So every suburb-page ISR (re)generation downloads the whole state to read one row. Sizes re-measured against prod today, matching the reviewer exactly: NSW 3,355,213 B / 4,544 rows (2.2 s), QLD 2,406,644 / 3,235, VIC 2,344,439 / 3,076; 15,541 rows total, 1,165 priced (VIC 739 + SA 426). The proposed fix is verified working: {"stateCode":"VIC","query":"abbotsford","limit":50} returns 1 row / 1,132 bytes (~2,000x smaller).

REFUTED (the mechanism, and the "all 8 states" claim). The 2 MB drop at web/node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/incremental-cache/index.js:386 is never reached. patch-fetch.js:389-395 builds the cache key first; connect-web passes body as a Uint8Array (connect-transport.js:81,84), and Next 14.2.13's fetchCacheKey (incremental-cache/index.js:227) tests `typeof init.body.keys === "function"` — true for TypedArrays — takes the FormData branch and throws `TypeError: formData.getAll is not a function` (simulated and reproduced). patch-fetch.js:392 swallows it, cacheKey stays undefined, and the incrementalCache.set at patch-fetch.js:456 is guarded off. So nothing is written for ANY state, not because of size. This is already recorded as landmine 0b in the repo's own memory (seo-competitive-strategy-2026-07.md: "default options -> Next tries to key streamed connect POST bodies ('Failed to generate cache key')"). By the reviewer's own stated mechanism, 5 of 8 states would have cached fine: SA 1.72 MB base64, WA 1.62, TAS 0.64, NT 0.31, ACT 0.13 — all under 2 MB.

NOT A REGRESSION. At base 8c120a352 web/src/app/housing/[state]/[suburb]/page.tsx read searchParams, so the route was fully dynamic and resolveSuburbSalCode ran the identical full-state pull on EVERY request — including the 404 path, since the base sitemap's slugifySuburb emitted trailing-hyphen slugs that suburbSlug never matched. The new generateStaticParams: () => [] + revalidate = 86400 + the tag cut that to once per URL per 24 h, i.e. 1-2 orders of magnitude less traffic than before. The reviewer's reading of the comment is also uncharitable: getHousing.ts:41-45 claims only that the tag is required so serverFetchWithUserAgent doesn't force cache:'no-store' and re-dynamise the route (true — see config.ts:255-266 shouldDisableFetchCache), not that the payload gets cached; the new test asserting the tag is passed is therefore asserting the invariant that actually matters.

UNVERIFIED sub-claim: the OG amplification is plausible — web/src/app/housing/[state]/[suburb]/opengraph-image.tsx exports revalidate = 86400 with no generateStaticParams (no OG route in the repo has one), matching recorded landmine 0a — but I could not confirm it live; prod returned 403 (Cloudflare) on the probe.

Bottom line for the parent: worth fixing as an efficiency item (narrow the resolution to a query= lookup, which would also make it data-cacheable), but it is a carried-forward inefficiency this PR reduces rather than a defect it introduces, and the write-path explanation in the finding should be corrected before it is repeated.

finding.title: OG logo tracing added for 3 of the 38 routes that read the logo from disk
finding.detail: The diff adds `./public/icon-512.png` + `./public/logo.png` to `outputFileTracingIncludes` for `/housing/[state]/opengraph-image`, `/housing/calculators/opengraph-image` and `/price-drops/opengraph-image`. The `readFile` that needs them lives in the shared `web/src/@/lib/og/card.tsx:54` (`for (const rel of ["public/icon-512.png", "public/logo.png"])`), which is imported by 38 opengraph-image routes (about, blog, compare, data, directory, economy, faq, glossary, industry-intelligence, insider-trading, learn, market, methodology, politicians x6, press, scans, screener, seasonality, shorts, statistics, top, ...). The other 35 lambdas still ship without the assets and fall through to the HTTP fallback at card.tsx:65-73 (`fetch(${siteUrl}/icon-512.png)`), adding a network round-trip per cold lambda and making the brand mark contingent on shorted.com.au being reachable from the OG lambda. The plan doc for this branch states the goal as "explicitly trace OG logo assets into every shared-card lambda"; the new `housing-og-tracing.test.ts` only asserts the three that were done, so it locks in the partial state.
finding.failure_scenario: A share of https://shorted.com.au/shorts/BHP is unfurled on a cold lambda: `getOgLogo()` misses both disk paths, falls back to fetching https://shorted.com.au/icon-512.png; if that request is slow, rate-limited or blocked, `cachedLogo` is memoised as "" for the lifetime of the instance and every card that instance renders ships with no brand mark.
finding.fix: Trace the two logo files for every route that imports `@/lib/og/card` (or add a single entry keyed on the shared chunk), and widen the test to enumerate the importers rather than a hardcoded list of three.

verdict.note:
Mechanism verified with build evidence, but the finding's exemplar and framing need correcting; it is a pre-existing gap, not a regression.

VERIFIED: web/src/@/lib/og/card.tsx:54 reads the mark via `for (const rel of ["public/icon-512.png","public/logo.png"]) readFile(join(process.cwd(), rel))`. 38 opengraph-image routes call getOgLogo (39 grep hits incl. card.tsx). The local build proves nft cannot resolve that loop: NO OG route .nft.json under web/.next/server/app contains any public/ entry. Decisive contrast: .next/server/app/api/og/twitter/[type]/route.js.nft.json DOES list "../../../../../../../public/assets/logo-small.png" because that route uses an inline literal (route.tsx:22-23). No other include mechanism exists (neither vercel.json has includeFiles). So the 35 untraced shared-card lambdas do hit the HTTP fallback, and cachedLogo="" is sticky (`if (cachedLogo !== null) return cachedLogo`).

CORRECTIONS: (1) The /shorts/BHP scenario is wrong — web/src/app/shorts/[stockCode]/opengraph-image.tsx does not import getOgLogo; it has a local getAssetBase64(path) reading public/assets/logo-small.png with `if (cachedLogo) return` (empty is NOT sticky), and the proposed fix would not cover it. Correct exemplars: /shorts (index), /statistics, /top, /politicians/*. (2) Not introduced here: base 8c120a352 had zero logo includes; all 38 routes were already in this state and the diff strictly improves 3. (3) The 3 added are precisely the housing-family routes that call getOgLogo (/housing/[state], /housing/calculators, /price-drops) — /housing/opengraph-image and /housing/[state]/[suburb] use scene JPEGs and never call it — so this housing branch covered 3/3 in-scope lambdas, even though docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-09-web-suburbs-completion.md:7 phrases the goal as "every shared-card lambda". (4) Cheaper fix than enumerating 38 keys: inline the two literals inside getOgLogo (the pattern proven to trace by the twitter route), or use a glob key such as "**/opengraph-image" in outputFileTracingIncludes.

SEVERITY: minor. Degradation is graceful (one extra same-origin fetch per cold instance; logo-less card only if that fetch fails), it is pre-existing on 35 routes rather than caused by this change, and the new housing-og-tracing.test.ts asserting only 3 routes matches the branch's actual scope.

finding.title: INGEST_ERROR check is unscoped — any operator-run mode's stale 'error' row pins the daily sentinel red forever
finding.detail: The first violation branch is `FROM house_price_ingest_runs AS r WHERE r.status = 'error'` with no join to `expected_fact_sources`, no source allowlist and no age bound. `house_price_ingest_runs` is NOT an official-ingest-only table: `updateRun(..., "error", ...)` is also written by the opt-in / operator-run modes — `crawl` (crawl.go:258, 294), `listings_rea`/`listings_domain` (crawl_listings.go:275, 292), `listing_details` (crawl_details.go:70, 89), `property_valuations` (crawl_property.go:83, 102), `crime_primaries` (crime.go:34-106), `backfill_address_key`, `abs_census`, `aec_federal`, `abs_lga`, `local_amenities`, `nbn_footprint`, `suburb_archetypes`, plus the VIC/FAG council loaders. Those modes are documented as "opt-in only, never part of the scheduled run" (main.go:68, 78) — nothing clears the row, so `status` stays `'error'` until a human re-runs that exact mode. The workflow's own comment at lines 36-37 claims the explicit map "excludes non-fact cursors such as listings and census" — that is only true for the PERIOD_REGRESSION branch. Cadence compounds it: the official ingest is MONTHLY (terraform/modules/house-price-collector/main.tf scheduler) but this sentinel runs DAILY, so one failed source on the 5th produces ~30 consecutive red runs + 30 webhook pages. This also breaks the exit-code design's backstop: `officialRunFatal` deliberately lets 15/16 official sources fail and still exit 0 (main.go:60-66, TF default 15), on the assumption this sentinel catches partial failures — a permanently-red sentinel catches nothing.
finding.failure_scenario: Someone runs `-mode crime` once (yearly, operator-run) and the BOCSAR download 404s → `crime_primaries` row is written with status='error' and is never touched again. From that day on, Housing Freshness exits 1 at 22:11 UTC every single day and POSTs to CRAWL_FRESHNESS_WEBHOOK, regardless of housing data health. The EVENT_SILENCE branch — the check that actually detects a dead residential rig within 72h, the thing this workflow exists for — produces no state change because the run was already red, so a dead rig goes unnoticed exactly as before.
finding.fix: Scope INGEST_ERROR to the same `expected_fact_sources` cursor list used by PERIOD_REGRESSION (or an explicit allowlist), and/or bound it by `r.last_fetched_at > now() - interval 'N days'` so a stale one-shot mode's cursor cannot pin the sentinel.

verdict.note:
CONFIRMED as described, at .github/workflows/housing-freshness.yml:82-91.

Verified chain:
1. The INGEST_ERROR arm is literally `FROM house_price_ingest_runs AS r WHERE r.status = 'error'` — no join to expected_fact_sources, no allowlist, no age bound. The explicit cursor map (lines 42-59) feeds only mapped_fact_maxima, which is used solely by the PERIOD_REGRESSION arm, so the "excludes non-fact cursors such as listings and census" comment at lines 36-37 does not apply to the first arm.
2. house_price_ingest_runs is a one-row-per-source cursor (migration 000053: `source TEXT PRIMARY KEY`; store.go:114-126 `ON CONFLICT (source) DO UPDATE ... status = EXCLUDED.status`). No TTL/trigger/cleanup exists in any migration, so a row's status persists until that exact source is written again.

finding.title: `-mode vg-nsw` reports success (exit 0, status='ok') when the newest NSW years are Cloudflare-blocked — the freshness gate is fooled by the thin-suburb pooled period
finding.detail:
The mode's stated contract (main.go:56-60 and deploy/README.md: "returns exit 1 on ingest/freshness failure ... launchd cannot report a silent success") is not met.

Three things combine:
1. `ingestNSWSuburbMedians` treats a per-year Cloudflare block as a SKIP (nsw_vg.go:69-76) and only errors when ALL three years fail (`if fetched == 0`, nsw_vg.go:100). One year out of three is enough to return observations.
2. The thin-suburb pooled fallback stamps its median at `latestYr` — `years[len(years)-1]`, computed from `nswRecentYears()` (nsw_vg.go:104-105) and NOT from the years actually fetched. So a run that only downloaded 2023.zip still emits `Period = 2025-12-31` for every thin suburb with >= 6 pooled sales (nsw_vg.go:130-133). NSW has thousands of low-turnover localities, so this always fires.
3. `assertOfficialVGFreshness` reads `MAX(period)` over the whole `house_prices` table for the source (official_freshness.go:24-29). That is monotonic (upserts never delete), and it is now equal to the fake 2025-12-31 stamp.

Result: `runOfficialJob` returns true -> `updateRun(vg_nsw, 2025-12-31, N, 'ok')` (main.go:424-426), `classifyVGFreshness` sees a period well inside the 550-day horizon and returns "", `runNSWVGRig` returns 0, the wrapper skips its osascript alert, and `refresh()` publishes MVs built from a 1-of-3-years corpus. Nothing in the pipeline compares this run's `latestPeriod(obs)` against the persisted cursor, so a regression is invisible by construction.
finding.failure_scenario: Rig runs `-mode vg-nsw` on the 8th. valuergeneral.nsw.gov.au serves the Cloudflare interstitial for 2025.zip and 2024.zip (logged "did not return a zip ... skipping") but 2023.zip downloads. Suburb medians are rebuilt from 2023 sales only; every thin suburb writes a 2023-derived median stamped `period = 2025-12-31`. `house_price_ingest_runs.vg_nsw` shows status='ok', last_period=2025-12-31; the process exits 0; launchd records success; `mv_housing_headline` is refreshed with two years of NSW suburb medians silently missing and 2023 prices published as 2025. The next Cloud Run `-mode all` freshness assertion also passes. No operator signal for 550 days.
finding.fix: Gate on the run's own coverage rather than the fact table's monotonic MAX: fail `-mode vg-nsw` when `fetched < len(nswRecentYears(nswYears))` (or at minimum when the newest complete year was not fetched), and stamp the pooled fallback at the newest year actually fetched, not `nswRecentYears()[last]`. Additionally compare `latestPeriod(obs)` against the persisted `house_price_ingest_runs.last_period` and treat a regression as an error.

verdict.note:
Defect is real and reachable; one factual correction to the reviewer's illustrative scenario.

CONFIRMED mechanics:
1. services/house-price-collector/nsw_vg.go:69-81 — a Cloudflare interstitial for a given year is a `continue` (skip); only `fetched == 0` returns an error (:100-102). Contrast: the VIC path in the same diff hard-fails on a block page (vic_vpsr.go).
2. nsw_vg.go:104-105,130-133 — the thin-suburb pooled fallback stamps `Period` at `latestYr = nswRecentYears(nswYears)[last]`, i.e. a year that may never have been fetched. Reproduced with a verbatim copy of the emit loop (/tmp/vgcheck): with 2023+2024 fetched and 2025 blocked, a 3+3-sale suburb emits `Period = 2025-12-31` from 2023/2024 sales.
3. store.go:84-112 upserts only (never deletes) so `MAX(period)` per source is monotonic; official_freshness.go:24-29,64-78 gates solely on that monotonic max vs a 550-day horizon. Nothing compares this run's `latestPeriod(obs)` to the persisted cursor — updateRun (store.go:114-123) overwrites `last_period` unconditionally, so a 2025->2024 regression is recorded as status='ok'. Grep confirms no coverage guard on `fetched` anywhere.

Result: runOfficialJob returns true -> runNSWVGRig (main.go:432-441) returns 0 -> deploy/run-housing-vg-nsw.sh:39-42 skips the osascript alert -> refresh() publishes MVs from a partial corpus. This violates the contract stated at main.go:56-60 and deploy/README.md ("If the residential run is challenged, leave the non-zero status/error row intact"). Two independent routes: (a) the run's own pooled rows stamped at latestYr satisfy the very freshness assertion that follows (self-fulfilling gate; near-certain to fire given the number of low-turnover NSW localities), and (b) any prior successful run's persisted 2025 period keeps the monotonic MAX green for ~550 days.

CORRECTION to the finding's FAILURE SCENARIO: the literal "only 2023.zip downloads" case is the one case where the fake stamp cannot occur. "Thin" means < nswMinSales (5) in every fetched year, so with a single fetched year pooled <= 4 < nswMinPooled (6) — the pooled branch never fires. Simulation output for 1-of-3 was `BIGTOWN@2023(annual)` only. So last_period would be 2023-12-31 (not 2025-12-31), and on a table with no newer period that run correctly exits 1 (2023-12-31 + 550d = 2025-07-04 < today). The reachable instantiation is "newest year blocked while >= 2 older years succeed", or any partial run following a prior run that persisted a newer period. The DETAIL's general statement of the mechanism is accurate; only its narrowest instantiation is not.

Scope note: the skip-on-block and pooled-at-latestYr behaviours are pre-existing in nsw_vg.go (the diff only reworded its comments); what this diff adds is the freshness gate + exit-code contract that those behaviours defeat. official_freshness.go and vg_nsw_runner_test.go are new here and neither test exercises partial-year coverage.

Severity: major stands — new load-bearing guard fails to detect the exact failure mode it was added for, and mis-vintaged medians (flagged is_preliminary, so partially mitigated) reach mv_housing_headline. Not a blocker: no crash, no security impact, well-traded suburbs keep correct years. go vet clean; focused tests (TestRunNSWVGRig, TestClassifyVGFreshness, TestNSWRecentYears, TestScheduledOfficialJobs) pass.

finding.title: The Cloud Run `-mode all` job now exits 1 for `vg_nsw`, a source it deliberately does not run — with max_retries=2 this re-runs the entire ABS/RBA/SA/VIC ingest 3x every month
finding.detail:
`scheduledOfficialJobs()` (main.go:366-386) intentionally drops `vg_nsw` because its challenge cannot clear from datacenter egress, but line 51 still asserts freshness over the FULL `vgFreshnessPolicies` list, which includes `vg_nsw` (official_freshness.go:18-22). With no `vg_nsw` rows in prod, `classifyVGFreshness` returns the "has never succeeded" branch (official_freshness.go:65-67), `enforceVGFreshness` sets exit 1, and `run()` returns 1 at line 54.

`terraform/modules/house-price-collector/main.tf:56` sets `max_retries = 2`, so a non-zero task exit is retried twice. Each attempt re-executes all 15 scheduled sources (ABS SDMX + RBA + CKAN + land.vic.gov.au fetches), plus `refresh()` -> `linkSuburbSalCodes` + `refresh_housing_materialized_views()` + `pingRevalidate` (main.go:341-364). So one monthly schedule becomes 3 full ingests, 3 prod MV refreshes and 3 ISR purges of /price-drops + /housing.

Secondary effect: the job's pass/fail signal no longer means "the sources I ran are healthy". A genuine ABS/RBA/VIC breakage is indistinguishable from "the residential Mac hasn't been set up yet", and the job is red from the moment this merges until someone installs and successfully runs the launchd job.
finding.failure_scenario: Merge lands; scheduler fires on the 5th at 16:00 UTC. runOfficial completes all 15 sources successfully, then `assertOfficialVGFreshness` logs "LOUD: vg_nsw house_prices has never succeeded" and `run()` returns 1. Cloud Run marks the task failed and retries twice -> 45 upstream source fetches, 3 `refresh_housing_materialized_views()` calls on prod Supabase and 3 revalidate pings in one scheduled window, and the job shows FAILED in the jobs dashboard indefinitely.
finding.fix: Assert only the policies for sources this invocation actually ran (pass a filtered list, mirroring what `runNSWVG` does at main.go:445-450), and surface the cross-source watchdog through the persisted `house_price_ingest_runs` row / job-monitoring rather than through the shared job's process exit code — or set `max_retries = 0` on the job so a data-freshness alarm doesn't triple the ingest.

verdict.note:
CONFIRMED as described, and prod state was verified rather than assumed.

MECHANISM (all re-read in the worktree):
- services/house-price-collector/main.go:49-55 — `case "official","abs","all"` calls `assertOfficialVGFreshness(ctx, pool, vgFreshnessPolicies)` with the FULL policy list, then `return 1`. The `policies` parameter exists specifically so a caller can scope it; `runNSWVG` (main.go:432-450) does filter to `nswSource`, the scheduled path does not.
- official_freshness.go:18-22 includes `{source:"vg_nsw", maxAgeDays:550}`; `scheduledOfficialJobs()` (main.go:366-386) deliberately omits `vg_nsw`, and vg_nsw_runner_test.go ASSERTS that omission. The scheduled job therefore enforces a policy it structurally cannot satisfy. No env gate, no build tag, no fallback anywhere in the diff.
- Scoped suite re-run green (10/10): `go test ./house-price-collector/ -run 'VGFreshness|ClassifyVG|EnforceVG|AssertVG|ScheduledOfficialJobs|RunNSWVGRig|CollectorTimeout' -v`. The tests themselves encode "never succeeded -> exit 1".

AMPLIFICATION (verified):
- terraform/modules/house-price-collector/main.tf:56 `max_retries = 2` => 3 total task attempts; the Cloud Run job uses the default Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT (`-mode all`).
- terraform/environments/prod/main.tf:185-196 sets `manage_revalidation_secret = true`, so REVALIDATION_SECRET IS mounted and `pingRevalidate` does not no-op (revalidate.go:29-35). Each attempt = 15 sources + `linkSuburbSalCodes` + `SELECT refresh_housing_materialized_views()` + /price-drops,/housing purge.
- Correct nuance: the scheduler's own `retry_count = 2` retries the `:run` API call, not the task, so the multiplier is 3x, not 9x — the finding attributed it correctly.

REACHABILITY (checked against prod via read-only public API, no credentials):
- ListStateSuburbs NSW (mosman/blacktown/parramatta): no `latestMedianPrice`/`latestPeriod` on any NSW suburb; only crawl-tier `SUBURB:NSW-<postcode>-<NAME>` region codes. SA = 2,775,000 @ 2026-06-30; VIC = 1,300,000 @ 2024-12-31 via `SUBURB:<ST>-<NAME>`.
- ListHousingRegions NSW returns only postcode-slug crawl regions; VIC returns `SUBURB:VIC-ABBOTSFORD...` with prices. nsw_vg.go:142 emits `SUBURB:NSW-<UPPER>` — absent from prod.
- The read path's only licence filter is `source_licence <> 'proprietary-tos-restricted'` (postgres_house_prices.go:320-324) and `nswLicence = "CC-BY"`, so vg_nsw could not be hidden by the gate.
=> prod has zero vg_nsw rows; `classifyVGFreshness(..., nil)` hits the "has never succeeded" branch on the first scheduled run after merge.

TWO FINDINGS THAT MAKE IT WORSE THAN WRITTEN:
1. prod `vg_vic` MAX(period) is 2024-12-31 = 587 days old vs the 550-day policy, so the shared job can exit 1 a second, independent way unless the new VIC dynamic workbook discovery lands a 2015-2025 file.
2. `nswRecentYears` only ever banks Dec-31-of-the-last-complete-year, so even a successful residential run buys at most ~18 months before the Cloud Run job goes red again — the coupling is a recurring time bomb, not a one-off.

SEVERITY: major (unchanged). Not data corruption or user-facing, but it leaves a deployed prod Cloud Run job permanently FAILED from the moment it merges, makes a genuine ABS/RBA/VIC breakage indistinguishable from "the residential Mac isn't set up" (the exact desensitisation pattern behind this repo's prior silently-red-job incidents), and triples the monthly ingest, prod Supabase MV refresh and ISR purge. The proposed fix (scope the assertion to the sources the invocation ran + surface the cross-source watchdog through `house_price_ingest_runs`/job-monitoring, and/or `max_retries = 0`) is the right shape.

finding.detail:
`selectVICWorkbookURL` seeds `bestEnd = -1` (line 67) and picks the maximum `end` year among links matching `houses-by-suburb-YYYY-YYYY.xlsx` (line 87). It never compares the winner against the pinned `vicXLSXURL` (2014-2024) or against the period already persisted for `vg_vic`.

`fetchVICSuburbWorkbook` only falls back to the pinned URL when discovery *errors* (lines 107-118). A discovery that succeeds with an older workbook short-circuits the fallback entirely: the bytes validate as xlsx (`validateVICXLSX`, line 139), `parseVICSuburbMedians` parses them, and `runOfficialJob` upserts every row. `upsertObservations` is `ON CONFLICT (region_code, measure, dwelling_type, period, source) DO UPDATE SET value = EXCLUDED.value` (store.go:90-93), so the older edition's numbers overwrite the current values for every overlapping suburb-year, and `updateRun` records status='ok' with a regressed `last_period` (main.go:424-426). Nothing compares the new max period to the stored cursor.

The new freshness gate cannot catch this either: it reads `MAX(period)` across all `vg_vic` rows (official_freshness.go:25-29), which still includes the untouched 2020-2024 rows, so it stays green.
finding.failure_scenario: land.vic.gov.au renames the current release (e.g. to `median-house-by-suburb-2025.xlsx`, or `houses-by-suburb-time-series.xlsx`) so the regex at vic_vpsr.go:38 misses it, while an "Earlier statistics" link to `houses-by-suburb-2013-2023.xlsx` remains on the page. Discovery returns the 2013-2023 archive; it fetches 200 and parses cleanly; the collector overwrites `house_prices` values for VIC suburbs across 2014-2023 with the older edition's medians, drops nothing for 2024, and writes `vg_vic` status='ok' last_period=2023-12-31. `/housing/vic/*` serves the regressed medians and neither the run row nor the freshness gate flags it.
finding.fix: Reject any discovered candidate whose end year is not greater than both the pinned fallback's end year (2024) and the persisted `house_price_ingest_runs.last_period` year; on rejection either fall through to the pinned URL or fail loudly. Also compare `latestPeriod(obs)` against the persisted cursor in `runOfficialJob` and treat a backwards move as an error rather than 'ok'.

verdict.note:
Core defect verified in /Users/benebsworth/projects/.worktrees/shorted-hw-collector-vg/services/house-price-collector/vic_vpsr.go, but one supporting claim is wrong and the severity is overstated.

CONFIRMED mechanics (all read directly):
1. vic_vpsr.go:66-91 — `bestStart, bestEnd := -1, -1` then `if end > bestEnd || (end == bestEnd && start > bestStart)`. No floor against the pinned `vicXLSXURL` (2014-2024, line 29) and no read of any persisted period. Any single matching link wins, however old.
2. vic_vpsr.go:99-126 — the pinned fallback is reached only when `discoveryErr != nil` OR the discovered fetch/`validateVICXLSX` fails. A discovery that succeeds and downloads a valid older xlsx returns at line 112 and never touches `vicXLSXURL`.
3. Reachable on the deployed path: `{"vg_vic", ingestVICSuburbMedians}` is in `scheduledOfficialJobs()` (main.go:385) and `.github/workflows/terraform-deploy.yml:283` builds `services/house-price-collector/Dockerfile` for the Cloud Run job. (The stale duplicate at services/jobs/internal/jobs/houseprices/vic_vpsr.go:40 still uses the pinned URL only and is not what deploys.)
4. store.go:85-93 `ON CONFLICT (region_code, measure, dwelling_type, period, source) DO UPDATE SET value = EXCLUDED.value` — the older edition's medians do overwrite overlapping suburb-years, and `runOfficialJob` (main.go:401-419) writes status='ok' with `latestPeriod(obs)` with no comparison to the stored cursor.
`go vet` clean; `go test -run 'VIC|VG|Freshness'` → 31 pass. No existing test asserts a year floor.

REFUTED sub-claim — "the freshness gate ... stays green": `vgFreshnessPolicies` sets vg_vic `maxAgeDays: 550` (official_freshness.go:21). In the reviewer's own scenario MAX(period) is pinned at 2024-12-31, and `classifyVGFreshness` goes LOUD once now > 2026-07-04 (arithmetic re-run). `assertOfficialVGFreshness` runs after `runOfficial` in the same process (main.go:50-55), its recorder calls `updateRun(..., "error", detail)` which OVERWRITES the vg_vic run row's status='ok' (store.go:114-121), and run() returns exit 1. So the missed new release IS flagged in the run row, the logs and the job exit code within <=550 days of the last good period. What the gate genuinely cannot see is the value regression: the untouched 2024 rows keep MAX(period) identical whether or not the stale workbook was ingested, so overwriting 2014-2023 medians with an older edition's numbers is silent. Also note nothing reads `house_price_ingest_runs.last_period` as a cursor (only writers found), so the "regressed cursor" is observability-only.

Severity re-graded major -> minor: it is a real robustness gap in newly-added code (and a regression from the previous pinned-URL-only behaviour, which failed loudly on a rename), but the harm needs a future upstream rename off `houses-by-suburb-YYYY-YYYY.xlsx` PLUS a surviving older archive link; today discovery cannot select below the pinned 2024 edition; the stale-VIC symptom is caught by the 550-day gate; and the residual undetected damage is a bounded historical-value regression that self-heals on the next successful newer-workbook ingest. The proposed fix (reject candidates whose end year is not > the pinned fallback's end year / persisted period, and treat a backwards `latestPeriod` as an error) is still the right hardening.

finding.failure_scenario: After merge, CI prints "Portal content provenance check passed (1750 scoped files scanned)" (I ran it) while `services/house-price-collector/crawl_listings_extract_test.go:134-139` still publishes a named real-estate agent + agency bound to `67 Alma Street, Paddington, Qld 4064` and a $2,310,000 price in a public repo — exactly the content class the commit exists to remove. finding.fix: Regenerate those two Go fixtures with the same synthetic vocabulary used for the HTML fixtures (Synthetic Suburb / ZZ 0000 / invented agency+agent strings — the parser is schema-agnostic so no assertion changes shape), and widen `isInScope` to all tracked files under `services/` plus the workflow `paths:` to `services/**`, with an explicit allowlist for the structural-shape fixtures that legitimately need `window.ArgonautExchange` / `__NEXT_DATA__` wrappers.

verdict.note:
CONFIRMED — both halves of the claim reproduce exactly, and the scope gap is worse than the reviewer stated.

**1. Residual content is real and untouched.** `git diff 8c120a352 -- services/house-price-collector/crawl_listings_extract_test.go` rewrites only the header comment and the two `TestExtractPageMeta_*` bodies. `TestHarvestListing_AgencyAndAgents` is not in the diff, and lines 130-141 still read verbatim:
```go

"price":          map[string]any{"display": "$2,310,000"},
"address":        map[string]any{"display": map[string]any{"fulladdress": "67 Alma Street, Paddington, Qld 4064"}},
"listingcompany": map[string]any{"id": "PRDPAD", "name": "Place - Paddington"},
"listers": []any{ {"name": "Tim Douglas"}, {"name": "Jane Smith"}, ... }
```
Identical at the same lines in `/Users/benebsworth/projects/.worktrees/shorted-hw-repo-hygiene/services/jobs/internal/jobs/houseprices/crawl_listings_extract_test.go`. Provenance corroborated: `git log -S'151008144'` points to 2f4a34f91 (#277, 2026-07-16), whose body says "Verified on a **REAL captured REA search page**" and quotes a neighbouring record from the same street ("24 Alma Street, Paddington | Brisbane Real Estate | JoJo Wu, Duane Preece"). The commit's newly-written header comment on this very file now asserts the fixtures are synthetic "without republishing portal payloads, listing data, or real-world identities" — false for its lower half. Sibling `crawl_listings_test.go:86-95` likewise still holds Domain ids 2019015084 / 2020346264 / 2020524930 with `9/285-295 Bondi Road`, prices, landSize and lat/lng -33.895/151.269.

**2. The gate provably cannot reach it — stronger evidence than the finding gives.** `scripts/check-portal-content-provenance.mjs:50` is `path.startsWith("web/") || (path.startsWith("services/") && path.includes("/testdata/"))`; `.github/workflows/repo-hygiene.yml:6` lists only `services/**/testdata/**` (+ `deploy/**`, `web/**`, docs, scripts) — a PR touching only `services/**/*.go` never starts the job. finding.title: The gate matches only three wrapper tokens, never the leaked content — renaming two identifiers re-lands the entire original capture with a green check
finding.detail: `signatures()` tests for `window.ArgonautExchange =`, `canonicalSearchId`, and (`__NEXT_DATA__` AND `totalListings:` AND `searchRequest:`). Every one of those is a cosmetic wrapper token, and none of the actually sensitive material — street addresses, suburb+postcode pairs, prices, listing ids, agent/agency names, `realestate.com.au/property-*` or `domain.com.au/...-<9-digit-id>` canonical URLs — is examined. Worse, this branch itself establishes the exact rename pattern that defeats the gate (`__NEXT_DATA__` → `__SYNTHETIC_DOMAIN_PAGE_META__`, `window.ArgonautExchange` → `window.SyntheticHousingPageMeta`), so the natural next move for someone hand-building a fixture from a live capture is to keep the real values and rename the wrapper. The Domain signature is also fragile in the other direction: it AND-requires `__NEXT_DATA__`, so a capture from any Domain page that moves off the Pages-Router bootstrap slips through even unmodified.
finding.failure_scenario: I reproduced it: `git show 8c120a352:services/house-price-collector/testdata/rea-pagemeta.html | sed -e 's/window.ArgonautExchange/window.SyntheticHousingPageMeta/' -e 's/canonicalSearchId/syntheticSearchId/' > $T/services/house-price-collector/testdata/rea-pagemeta.html; node scripts/check-portal-content-provenance.mjs --root $T` → "Portal content provenance check passed (1 scoped files scanned)", exit 0 — while that file still contains `33/75 Welsby Street, New Farm, Qld 4005`, `12 Moray Street, New Farm, Qld 4005`, listing ids 151775764/151774984 and the canonical URLs `https://www.realestate.com.au/property-apartment-qld-new+farm-151775764`. finding.fix: Add content signatures alongside the wrapper ones — e.g. `realestate\.com\.au/property-[a-z]`/`domain\.com\.au/[a-z0-9-]+-\d{9,}` canonical listing URLs, `"(fullAddress|shortAddress|streetAddress)"\s*:\s*"\d+[/\- ]` (a numbered street address), and a real-postcode+state pair — since those are the fields that constitute the leak and survive any wrapper rename. verdict.note:
CONFIRMED with one correction to the repro. The core claim is true: scripts/check-portal-content-provenance.mjs:93-105 `signatures()` tests only three wrapper tokens (`window.ArgonautExchange =`, `canonicalSearchId`, and `__NEXT_DATA__` AND `totalListings:` AND `searchRequest:`); no address / postcode / price / listing-id / canonical-URL signature exists anywhere in the branch (grepped the full diff for `address|postcode|street|price|realestate\.com|domain\.com` — only the generator's synthetic `postCode: "0000"` and two allow-case attribution hyperlinks in the tests). I reproduced the reviewer's command verbatim: the renamed 8c120a352 REA capture in a temp root yields "Portal content provenance check passed (1 scoped files scanned)", exit 0, while still containing `33/75 Welsby Street, New Farm, Qld 4005`, `12 Moray Street, ...`, ids 151775764/151774984 and `https://www.realestate.com.au/property-apartment-qld-new+farm-151775764`. MISSED GUARD (invalidates the reviewer's specific path): the same workflow step runs scripts/tests/portal-content-provenance.test.mjs, whose final test byte-compares all four committed fixtures against fresh generator output. In a minimal fake repo I confirmed that re-landing the renamed capture at services/house-price-collector/testdata/rea-pagemeta.html leaves the checker green (exit 0, "4 scoped files scanned") but turns the suite red (pass 9 / fail 1) — so CI does catch that exact scenario. STILL REACHABLE: on any OTHER in-scope path there is no guard at all. Same fake repo with the renamed REA capture written to a NEW file services/house-price-collector/testdata/rea-pagemeta-page2.html plus a Domain capture (`__NEXT_DATA__` -> `__SYNTHETIC_DOMAIN_PAGE_META__`) under web/src/__fixtures__/ gives: checker "passed (6 scoped files scanned)" exit 0 AND all 10 hygiene tests pass, with `"street":"312 Bowen Terrace"`, `"postcode":"4005"`, `"price":"$1,050,000"` and listing ids 2019981372/2020997876 committed. Before this branch there was no gate and the real captures were committed; the branch deletes them, adds the gate, and double-guards the four canonical fixtures. The residual hole requires a human to deliberately hand-commit a wrapper-renamed capture at a new path.
